newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Japanese diplomat wins Magsaysay prize.
newsitem.headline: Japanese diplomat wins Magsaysay prize.

text.p: Japan's Sadako Ogata, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), on Wednesday was named the winner of the Ramon Magsaysay award for international understanding for easing the misery of refugees around the world.
The Magsaysay board of trustees also cited the Japanese diplomat for her success in repatriating hundreds of thousands of Burmese, Cambodian and Vietnamese refugees to their homeland.

She invoked "the moral authority of the UNHCR to insist that behind the right of every refugee to asylum lies the greater right of every person to remain at home in peace", the board said in its citation.
Ogata was the fifth Magsaysay awardee this year.

She and the other winners each are to receive a cash prize of $50,000 and a medallion in ceremonies in Manila on August 31 to commemorate the birth anniversary of Ramon Magsaysay, a popular Philippine president who died in an air crash in 1957.

The other winners were former Thai prime minister Anand Panyarachun for government service, Indian environmental crusader Mahesh Chander Mehta for public service, Filipino nun Eva Fidela Maamo for community leadership, and Indian writer Mahasweta Devi for literature.
At UNHCR, Ogata presided over the return to their countries of 200,000 Burmese Moslems, more than 70,000 Vietnamese and thousands of Cambodians, the board said.
"A key to success in such programmes has been Ogata's insistence that the UNHCR be permitted to monitor the experience of returnees against reprisal and discrimination," it said.
"Some 27 million displaced people now rely upon the UNHCR to protect their rights to asylum and to provide humanitarian relief. They are High Commissioner Ogata's responsibility."
